steps.content: After dinner, under the light of the campfire, Vanilla is repairing the damage on your armor.

After the sun sets, the temperature gradually drops. If not for the heat provided by the campfire, the chill would strip away all your warmth. The crackling flames, accompanied by the chirps of insects, paint a peaceful scene before your eyes...
But you are distracted, thinking about the sights you saw today and racking your brain for a foolproof way to break through.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: You've been to some very dangerous places, haven't you?
Vanilla knocks at the horrifying scratches on the armor. Her tone remains flat, but you can detect a hint of worry.

options: I'll protect it better next time.

steps.content: Vanilla shakes her head; that's not what she wants to hear.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: What happened?
You don't immediately answer her, but your gaze unconsciously drifts toward the mech on the other side.

options: How's the progress on the mech?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: If we calculate by working hours, it's about 75% finished.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...In that case, it shouldn't take too long, right?
Hearing your words, Vanilla stops her work and raises her head to look at you.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: You seem anxious. What happened?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: That day over the call, I remember you said you saw something?
Even Vanilla, who isn't very sensitive, has noticed your mood.
It's just her usual tone and way of speaking, but seeing how causally she brings it up, it unexpectedly evoke your desire to confide.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I saw monsters, lots and lots of them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And behind them, there's the light and storm, and the shadow within it... All of them seem to be preventing someone from approaching...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's not just that. This entire space, it seems to be created to trap someone. Leaving here isn't as simple as I thought.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Honestly, I'm not so sure anymore.
Vanilla quietly listens to you. After a while, she walks away from the workbench, and sits down next to you.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: That's some useful intel, with this, we now have an accurate assessment of our enemy.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: We just need to make the necessary adjustments and ensure the improved design can handle those issues.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: As long as we keep making progress on the mech at our current speed, and be well-prepared when we set out, there's nothing to be anxious about.
There's no sentimental comfort, nor any ingenious strategy. She just gave a simple analysis of the current situation and solutions to the predicament.
Strangely, these words bring comfort to your mind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm glad you're here...
Vanilla nods quietly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Speaking of, you're always so calm. I don't think I've ever seen you get anxious.
As you speak jokingly, you gaze at the peculiar scenery in the distance.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't you afraid of this place?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Not really, because nothing really changed for me.
Vanilla answers in her usual calm tone, but her words make you tense up a bit.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Nothing changed?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Yeah.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Before I joined the expedition, I worked at an outpost near the DisSea and lived there alone for ten years.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: There's no difference between here and the outpost.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Out there, there are no temporal storms, or abnormal timestream. People come and go, and things change. I would have thought...

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: ...For ten years, I looked at the same scenery every day: the desolate DisSea beach, the silent storm, the same sunrise and sunset. Same everything for ten years.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Humans can no longer change the world, for the world has been changed by the Perishing Star, and humans are now the ones being changed by the world. Everyone has the same look in their eyes, and to them, every day is the same.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: Those travelers came from all over the world, but they all had the same look in their eyes, just like mine. Those were the eyes dyed by this desolate scenery. Each of their days was just like the last.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: If there is such a thing as eternity, that must have been it...
Vanilla looks up at the sky, her voice soft and ethereal.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: So whether it's the outpost, or this camp, it's all the same.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: All I see is an unchanging scenery. There's no sign of humans, and no sight of the future. Disasters seem to be imminent, yet they never arrive.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: It's as if time has stopped itself, and the world has stopped changing.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: When I think like this, the temporal storms, and the chaotic time just can't scare me anymore.
Vanilla calmly recounts her experiences. The desolation has given her resilience, rationality, and wisdom.
But she seems to have forgotten how to embrace change.
How long have you been in this storm?
She thinks for a moment before answering.

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: I lost count.
...Do you want to leave with me?

steps.speaker: Vanilla
steps.content: You said you want to leave. I just want to help you.

options: What about you? Do you want to leave?

steps.content: Vanilla doesn't answer, her expression as calm as ever.
You've always believed that you could bring her back, but right now, you're not so sure anymore.
This is a storm of Mania. How can someone, who has no hope for the future nor desire to change, break through this storm?
